sources.title: NASA-STD-5001B with Change 3 — Structural Design and Test Factors of Safety for Spaceflight Hardware
sources.locator: Document Scope; version B with Change 3, active summary
sources.verified_summary: The standard addresses structural design, test, and service-life factors used in spaceflight hardware development and verification.
sources.design_application: Define a project-approved load, strength, test, and life basis for structures, joints, tank supports, and landing-load paths.
sources.limits: The source does not select our materials, factors, geometry, loads, or life. Citing it does not establish compliance or structural qualification.

sources.title: NASA-STD-5012C — Strength and Life Assessment Requirements for Liquid-Fueled Space Propulsion System Engines
sources.locator: Document Scope; version C, active summary
sources.verified_summary: The standard addresses engine structural strength and life, including fatigue and creep, through analyses and tests. It does not cover all system requirements for engine hot-fire testing.
sources.design_application: Separate engine structural/life evidence from complete propulsion-system performance and integration evidence; retain serial-number life records.
sources.limits: It is not an engine construction guide or proof that an engine has been selected. No operational values or test procedures were copied.

sources.title: Thermal Protection Materials Branch — Reusable Materials
sources.locator: Reusable TPS overview and material-system examples
sources.verified_summary: NASA describes reusable TPS, including servicing, material combinations, attachment systems, and application-dependent capability.
sources.design_application: Evaluate surface material, joints, attachments, thermal gradients, repeated exposure, inspection, repair, and replacement as one subsystem.
sources.limits: Listed heritage materials and temperatures are not rocketstar material choices, operating limits, or evidence of upper-stage reentry capability.

sources.title: ECSS-E-ST-33-01C Rev.2 — Mechanisms
sources.verified_summary: The standard covers spacecraft and payload mechanism definition, design, analysis, development, production, verification, and operation. Launcher applicability is left to the launcher project.
sources.design_application: Use mechanism specifications, design descriptions, analysis, tests, and operating constraints to structure retained-door and payload-separation interfaces.
sources.limits: Do not assert automatic launcher applicability, compliance, or approved separation/door design.

sources.title: GSFC-STD-7000B — General Environmental Verification Standard
sources.verified_summary: GEVS provides guidance for environmental verification of GSFC payloads, subsystems, and components using tests and/or analysis against expected mission environments.
sources.design_application: Define configuration-specific environment verification and affected-function retests after repair, component replacement, or interface change.
sources.limits: Guideline levels are not rocketstar qualification values and are not automatically applicable to a reusable launch vehicle or every refurbishment.

sources.title: Appendix D — Requirements Verification Matrix
sources.verified_summary: The matrix approach links uniquely identified requirements to verification methods and evidence.
sources.design_application: Tie configuration, interface revision, numerical acceptance criteria, test results, deviations, and release decisions to requirement IDs.
sources.limits: A populated matrix or a defined requirement is not evidence that testing passed or that flight approval exists.
